memories.content: Keep the total, major cost categories, and one-line estimate basis in the main text so the resource argument can be understood without leaving the proposal.
Place each major cost beside the activity or deliverable it enables in the main text.
State the quantity and unit-rate basis for each major cost in the same paragraph that requests it.
Readers may question a proposed priority when its cost cannot be checked on the same page as the claimed benefit.
Update the cost sentence whenever the related activity changes so the narrative and requested amount cannot drift apart.
Accept a denser main-text paragraph when the estimate basis is essential to deciding whether the request is proportionate.
The user tends to revise the work plan but forget a detached budget table unless the key amount is repeated beside the activity.
Calculate user research compensation budgets based on the estimated participation burden, combining session time with required technical and travel preparation.
Compensate participants who withdraw from the study midway for their actual participation time.
Compensate for the time actually spent in sessions, regardless of the research modality.
Allow the issuance of gift cards of equivalent value to participants in remote studies who cannot use electronic transfers.
Do not treat an unresolved payment method as a deficiency at the proposal stage.
Allow differential compensation amounts for on-site and remote studies when participation burden varies due to travel or technical preparation.
Participants judge the fairness of compensation based on the combined burden of session time and required technical and travel preparation.
In longitudinal studies requiring diary entries and repeated reporting, include out-of-session recording time in compensation calculations.
Distinguish between participant research compensation and labor costs for field staff performing installation and operational support as part of their duties.
The user tends to count session time but omit participants’ advance setup and follow-up reporting time.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate dimensions of research budgeting. The reference frame governs how costs and estimate bases stay visible and synchronized in proposal prose, while the compared frame governs participant-compensation calculation, fairness, payment flexibility, and cost classification.

relations.reason: This is a one-sided proposal-presentation policy; the compared frame addresses how participant compensation is determined rather than where budget justification appears.
relations.summary: Keep decision-essential cost totals, categories, and estimate bases in the main text even when this makes the prose denser.

relations.reason: This is a one-sided navigability and checkability claim without a corresponding compensation-policy claim in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Place major costs beside the activities or benefits they support so readers can assess cost against value on the same page.

relations.reason: This specific proposal-detail placement requirement appears only in the reference frame.
relations.summary: State each major cost’s quantity and unit-rate basis in the paragraph requesting it.

relations.reason: These memories express the same one-sided maintenance concern about plan-budget drift; the compared frame does not address document synchronization.
relations.summary: Keep activity descriptions and their nearby key amounts synchronized to prevent revisions from leaving a detached budget inconsistent with the work plan.

relations.reason: These memories state and motivate the same one-sided burden-based calculation principle, which the reference frame does not supply.
relations.summary: Base participant compensation on burden beyond session time, including applicable preparation, travel, setup, and follow-up work.

relations.reason: This withdrawal-specific compensation rule appears only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Compensate participants who withdraw midway for the time they actually participated.

relations.reason: This modality-neutral rule for session-time compensation appears only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Compensate actual session time regardless of whether participation is remote or on-site.

relations.reason: This conditional payment-method alternative appears only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Permit equivalent-value gift cards for remote participants who cannot use electronic transfers.

relations.reason: This proposal-stage evaluation rule appears only in the compared frame and is independent of the reference frame’s cost-presentation requirements.
relations.summary: Do not treat an unresolved payment method as a proposal-stage deficiency.

relations.reason: This conditional rule for differential compensation appears only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Allow on-site and remote compensation amounts to differ when their travel or technical-preparation burdens differ.

relations.reason: This longitudinal-study calculation rule appears only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Include out-of-session diary and repeated-reporting time when calculating compensation for longitudinal studies.

relations.reason: This cost-classification distinction appears only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Separate participant research compensation from labor costs for field staff performing installation or operational support.

reports.compared_only: Participant compensation should reflect actual and ancillary burden, including withdrawal, preparation, travel, and longitudinal reporting, while allowing suitable payment methods, burden-based modality differences, and separation from staff labor costs.
reports.reference_only: Proposal prose should expose decision-relevant totals, categories, unit-rate bases, and activity-linked costs, with related amounts updated as plans change.
